note: RULE ERROR in drift.ts, the wetness drift: `pull` reads only temperature and wind, so a waterlogged clay bed (mass 5, size 4) and a cloth shirt dry at the identical rate and both are bone dry in 36 hours; the scenario needs the clay to stay waterlogged for days. General rule: drying should slow with bulk and absorbency and quicken with porosity and exposed surface. Also missing: the second and third can are consumed and vanish ('the liquid runs off it'), so three cans equal one.

note: RULE ERROR in drift.ts, the contamination drift: `damp = 0.4 + 0.6 * wetness / 5` never falls below 0.4, so a bone-dry seed (perishability 1) on a cold shelf reaches contamination 5 in under two months, and in two weeks at mild temperature: noxious and stinking, a total loss, where the scenario has old dry seed merely weaker. The vocabulary (S9, S11) says dryness kills or slows rot. General rule: growth needs damp above a threshold; at wetness 0 it should be nil or near it, which is also what makes dried food keep. The patchy stand itself is unbuilt.

Turf with stone at abundance 2: a one-minute glance has 2% odds and finds nothing, no stone is made, and 45 deliberate minutes reach 60% without being sure. The glance is recorded as one searched minute, which costs the next search about 3%: close enough to 'not yet marked as searched'.

needs: a piece coming away from a large brittle thing (a share of the parent, not all of it)
depletion proportional to the stock a level stands for
composite instruments (chisel driven by hammer)
move (take)
care reaching force
note: Finding stone derives (70% at a glance, 97% in three minutes, far above turf). Two RULE ERRORS. (1) force.ts `damage`: `shatters = p.toughness <= 1 && met.blow > 1` ignores size, so one effort-3 hammer blow sets a size-5 rock face to integrity 0 ('it goes to pieces') while an effort-2 blow takes 0.006 off it and frees nothing; general rule: a blow that beats a brittle thing breaks off a share scaled by the blow against its bulk and creates that piece, and only a thing small against the blow shatters whole. (2) body.ts `searchOdds`: `level = abundance - found * 0.5` is linear in a scale whose rates are geometric, so a quarry's three-minute odds fall from 0.97 to 0.54 after one block, to 0.18 after three, and to zero for ever after nine; the minutes discount does the same to a place where stone is everywhere. General rule: each find, and each minute of ground gone over, should deplete in proportion to the stock the level stands for, so a grass patch gives out after one or two and a quarry does not give out by hand.

needs: yield that scales with time searched (a count or an amount)
search reading size, cover, light, acuity and attention (X8)
note: Odds derive: 8% at a glance, 98% in 45 minutes on a good patch, 17% on a thin one, never certain. RULE ERROR in body.ts `search`: `found = draw < odds ? 1 : 0` whatever the minutes, so an hour's careful search yields exactly one mushroom while the same hour typed as sixty glances yields five; the scenario expects several for the hour. General rule: the number found is drawn from rate times effective minutes, capped by the stock, and made as a count, so the yield depends on time spent and not on how the time is cut into acts. Also missing: a small mottled thing under leaf litter is exactly as easy to spot as a stone of the same abundance, because search reads abundance alone.

Abundance 0, or no entry at all, gives odds of exactly 0 however long and however often; ten two-hour searches make nothing and record 1200 minutes spent. Stone in the same stream is found readily, so it is the place's row and not the search that says no.

needs: an instrument and a manner for search (bait, rod)
ids for created things that are unique for the life of the world
a found thing taking its place's state (a caught fish is dry and mild)
size of what is found as a latent draw
move (cast, take)
note: Odds build with time on the line (10% in five minutes, 84% in ninety, never 1), which derives. Two RULE ERRORS in body.ts. (1) `searchOdds`: `fresh = minutes / (1 + before.minutes / 30)` discounts ground gone over only between acts and never within one, so two hours' waiting is 0.91 as one act, 0.80 as two and 0.65 as twelve; the player who types 'wait' more often catches less, and the player who declares one long search escapes the re-search penalty of find-06 altogether. General rule: make effective minutes a function of total minutes, 30 * ln((30 + before + minutes) / (30 + before)), which is the same curve and is invariant under splitting. (2) `search` names the find by element and the present count of things in the world: catch two fish, eat the first, catch a third, and the third is created as fish.1 over the fish.1 already there, leaving one fish where there should be two. General rule: ids come from a counter the world carries or from the logged act, never from the present count. Bait changes nothing because search takes no instrument. Unsure of one thing: whether waiting for a fish that swims should be discounted as ground gone over at all; the rule assumes a static stock.
